text_observations: Checkout error-rate alert fired at 10:04 UTC
Deployment dep-1842 for checkout-api completed at 10:01 UTC
Database latency increased at approximately the same time as the alert
External payment provider reported intermittent errors
A previous incident with similar symptoms involved an expired service credential
The incident director is asking about likely cause and rollback decision
The incident brief contains initial reports, not confirmed timeline or root cause
image_observations: Checkout error rate changed from 0.4% to 9% between approximately 10:01 and 10:03
Deploy dep-1842 occurred at 10:01 UTC (marked with dashed line)
Alert fired at 10:04 UTC (marked with dotted line)
Database p99 latency increased from 120ms to 850ms between 10:01 and 10:03
Failure breakdown at 10:05 shows: DB timeout 62%, Provider 5xx 27%, Validation 4%, Other 7%
inferred_conclusions: The deployment at 10:01 appears temporally correlated with both the error rate increase and database latency spike, suggesting the deployment may have introduced a problem
Database timeouts account for the majority (62%) of failures, indicating database performance degradation is the primary failure mode
The combination of high database latency (850ms p99) and high timeout failure rate suggests database queries may have become inefficient or resource-constrained after the deployment
The external payment provider errors (27% of failures) may be secondary effects caused by timeout cascades from the database issues
The timing sequence (deployment 10:01 → latency spike → error rate spike by 10:03 → alert 10:04) suggests a causal chain originating from the deployment
uncertainty: Whether the deployment itself introduced a code issue causing slow queries, or if it triggered an existing database performance problem; whether the expired service credential mentioned in the previous incident is relevant to this incident; whether rolling back would resolve the issue or if database-level intervention is needed; the exact nature of the database queries or operations affected by the deployment.
